chapter: Billy Hicks, the Apollo and Roy Eldridge
title: Nine months with Roy: the Arcadia, a tour to Detroit and the Apollo
summary: The Arcadia's waltz-tango-jazz format, broadcasts, the Graystone Ballroom in Detroit, and a full Apollo show.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Panama, we were talking about -- and you can hear the Florida rain and thunder coming in in the background -- now we talked about New York and we talked about Roy's band -- how long did you stay with Roy's band, Panama?
I stayed with Roy's band -- oh, let's see ... approximately six months I was with Roy. No, exactly 9 months I was with Roy, to be exact.
Okay, can you continue with that?
During the time I was with Roy, we were playing at the Arcadia Ballroom which was located on 53rd Street and Broadway.

The Arcadia was sort of like a dancing school, in a way. We had hostesses there. We used to play, like, 15 minutes of waltzes and then 15 minutes worth of tangos and 15 minutes worth of jazz -- this is the way it was all mapped out for the night.
And we used to broadcast from there; in fact, the first real broadcasting I ever did was from the Arcadia while I was with Roy.

And after we left the Arcadia, we went on a tour as far west as Detroit -- it was my first time playing at the Graystone Ballroom, and I had heard so much talk about the Graystone -- it was really a big thrill for me to be playing in the Graystone Ballroom.

So when we came back to New York, we opened at the Apollo Theatre, and now this was my first time also playing a real show with chorus girls and boys, and comedians and all of this, and I think I spoke about it a little before when I mentioned Tom Whaley telling me about how to play a show.
